subject: International transfer questionnaire, DPA redlines, and e-sign plan
messages:
From: Emma White <emma.white@asterbank.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@asterbank.com, Oleg Kovalenko <oleg.kovalenko@legalpartners.io>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA questions + transfer impact details

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for sending over the DPA redlines last week. We had our outside counsel skim the changes and have three items that need clarification before we can proceed to esign:

1) SCCs / UK IDTA: Your redline replaces the standard SCC attachment with a reference to a "Redwood transfer profile". We need confirmation whether that profile includes the latest 2024 SCCs mapping and a UK IDTA addendum — counsel is asking for explicit incorporation language.

2) Subprocessors: the redline narrows notification timing to "reasonable notice". For banking data we typically need 30 days for high-risk subprocessors — can you confirm whether Redwood will accept a 30-day notice window for any subprocessor handling EEA/UK personal data?

3) Transfer impact assessment (TIA): please provide the TIA that was used to justify the proposed transfer mechanism (or confirm that the attached assessment is the correct one). Our DPIA team flagged two entries on TLS/cross-region replicates that need comment.

We're trying to keep DocuSign routing simple — procurement would like a single signature pass if possible. Can you confirm your preferred esign provider (DocuSign/Adobe) and whether Redwood can pre-populate the signature blocks to include entity and signatory details?

Attached: AsterBank_DPA_redline_v3.docx (their redlines w/ comments).

If helpful, Oleg from our counsel looped in — he can take a look at any additional language you propose. Would appreciate a quick run-through by EOD Wednesday PT so we can hit our quarter close.

Best,
Emma
Head of Legal Operations
AsterBank

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Emma White <emma.white@asterbank.com>, Oleg Kovalenko <oleg.kovalenko@legalpartners.io>

Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA questions + transfer impact details

Emma — thanks, got this and the attached redlines.

Quick answers up front:
- SCCs / UK IDTA: Redwood intends to incorporate the 2024 EU SCCs and the UK IDTA addendum by reference; we call this the "Redwood transfer profile". We'll draft explicit incorporation language to make that clear for your counsel.
- Subprocessors: Our standard is notification and 15 days to review; for high-risk financial subprocessors we can accept a 30-day notice window as an exception with an entry in the subprocessor appendix.
- TIA: attaching the transfer_impact_assessment_AsterBank.pdf — this is the assessment our compliance team completed for AsterBank's configuration, with notes on TLS, replica regions, and data residency controls.

Plan: I'll loop legal (Marissa) and controls (Rishi/Mina) to confirm proposed wording. We should be able to produce a redline that adds explicit SCC/IDTA incorporation and a short subprocessor notice clause by tomorrow.

On e-sign: Redwood supports DocuSign and AdobeSign. DocuSign is preferred for account-level templates; we can pre-populate signatory blocks and route procurement -> legal in a single pass. I'll propose a DocuSign routing link once we confirm final signers.

Action items for us:
- Marissa: craft explicit incorporation paragraph for SCCs+UK IDTA (will include fallback language).
- Rishi + Mina: confirm the TIA notes and the 30-day subprocessor exception feasibility.
- Kimberly: coordinate final DocuSign template and provide a pre-signed sender address.

I'll follow up with an internal thread shortly with suggested text.

Thanks — Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 08:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: internal: DPA language ideas for AsterBank (draft below)

Kimberly / team — draft language and notes below. Please review quickly; will post a tracked redline after edits.

--- DRAFT PARAGRAPH (for insertion into DPA attachment A - Transfers):
"The Parties agree that the transfer mechanisms described in the Redwood Transfer Profile (incorporated by reference and available at [link]) comprise the appropriate safeguards for transfers of Personal Data from the European Economic Area and the United Kingdom to jurisdictions outside those territories. Where applicable, the 2024 Standard Contractual Clauses (EU) and the United Kingdom International Data Transfer Addendum (UK IDTA) shall be incorporated into this Agreement by reference and shall govern transfers to the extent they apply. In the event of any conflict between the Redwood Transfer Profile and the SCCs/UK IDTA, the SCCs/UK IDTA shall prevail to the extent required by Applicable Data Protection Law."

Notes: this makes the SCC/IDTA explicit and gives counsel the contractual certainty they asked for. We add a fallback precedence clause which is typically acceptable.

--- Subprocessor notice clause (proposed appendix language):
"For Subprocessors that may process Personal Data subject to EEA/UK law, Redwood shall give Data Controller no less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice of the appointment of any such Subprocessor, except where such notice is not reasonably practicable (in which case Redwood shall provide notice as soon as reasonably practicable). The parties may agree in writing to shorten the notice period for specific Subprocessors. For Subprocessors deemed high-risk by Controller, the parties will coordinate remedial controls and may require written consent prior to appointment."

Rishi / Mina — the technical TLS and cross-region items are addressed in the attached TIA doc where we note default encryption in transit, HSM for keys, and regional replication only on customer request. If there are gaps flagged by Aster's DPIA team, call them out and we'll propose mitigations.

If this looks good, Kimberly, I'll incorporate into a tracked redline and push back to Emma + Oleg with a short note and the TIA attached.

-Marissa
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Emma / Oleg — thanks for the patience. Please find attached: (1) Redwood redline with explicit SCCs/UK IDTA incorporation, (2) Transfer Impact Assessment used for AsterBank, and (3) a short redline summary. Key points below.

- SCCs/UK IDTA: We added explicit incorporation language into Attachment A and a conflict-resolution sentence to ensure the SCCs/IDTA carry force where applicable. This should address your counsel's request for explicit reference.
- Subprocessors: We have agreed to a 30-day notice window for EEA/UK-impacting subprocessors and added a high-risk consent carve-out in the subprocessor appendix (appendix B). We also included a brief process for expedited review if procurement needs a quicker path.
- TIA: the attached TIA calls out TLS, HSM key management, and configurable replication. Rishi and Mina confirmed the technical mitigations.

E-sign plan: We will use DocuSign. Proposed routing: Procurement (AsterBank) -> AsterBank Legal (Oleg) -> Redwood Contracts (Marissa) -> Redwood Legal (Kimberly). I can pre-populate signatory details on our DocuSign template and send as a single envelope. Once you confirm signers and order, I'll initiate the envelope and share the DocuSign link.

Next steps for you:
- Confirm the procurement/legal signatory order and whether Procurement wants a countersignature field for bank entity name.
- Confirm acceptance of the 30-day subprocessor notice and high-risk carve-out.

If Oleg wants to propose final tweaks, we can accept redline comments directly in DocuSign or via a final tracked Word document — whichever is easiest.

Thanks — look forward to closing this week.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
